newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends barely higher after choppy day.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends barely higher after choppy day.

text.p: COMEX copper ended slightly higher after a nervous, choppy session as the market remained uncertain of its direction following a smaller-than-expected rise in LME stocks and lingering worries about Wednesday's LME options declaration, traders said.
LME stocks rose 1,000 tonnes to 93,475 tonnes Tuesday. Traders had expected a hike of 2,000 to 3,000 tonnes.

Last week, there were worries about turmoil in copper as Wednesday's LME options declaration approached. These fears have largely subsided by now, said Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities. "It created unease and kept people out of the market," she added.
Most-active March settled 0.55 cent higher at 100.65 cents a lb after trading from 101.40 to 98.80 cents. Spot December closed 0.55 cent lower at 105.05 cents.
Volume was modest at an estimated 12,000 lots against Monday's official tally of 11,984 contracts.
The cash to three months backwardation on LME weakened earlier but firmed by the close to $163/$167, though still down from last week's much higher levels.

U.S. new home sales, a key consuming sector, fell 8.7 percent in October. The sharp drop to an annualized rate of 714,000 units was greater than analysts' predictions, but was seen as an overdue correction, bringing data in line with other soft housing sector indicators, economists said.
